And the people who were supposed to be sacrificed for the benefit of obtaining NATO intervention, they were the ones who remained in Srebrenica. That's what I was trying to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you know about Srebrenica at this time, 2013? Do you still claim that you know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I know almost everything about it, but not as a person who participated in its -- in it personally, but as a person who made an effort to try and find out what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you of the -- are you still of the view that it was organised by the Muslims themselves?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still think that this was organised by the Muslims with the help of their masters - and I'm not going to name them here - whereas the crime itself was committed by the Serb forces, but this was organised by Muslims plus someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What did you refer to when it was organised by the Muslims? You mean the killing of Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the operation against Srebrenica. So Srebrenica was a safe area, but it was not demilitarised. And there were persistent combat operations launched from Srebrenica in order to provoke an operation against Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question has consistently been about the fate of Muslim able-bodied men who are allegedly missing. So the question was about the death of those able-bodied men. Do you say that it was organised by the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims organised and provoked this entire operation, but the killing of these people was committed by the Serb forces as a consequence of what had been organised, because it was never the objective to accomplish peace in that area, to demilitarise Srebrenica and seize with combat operations. It was necessary to provoke the Serb side so that they would launch an operation that would lead to casualties, and it was well known that they knew that there would be casualties, because in -- in Srebrenica there were people who were encircled, and in the brigades that attacked -- that were attacking, there were people who had lost their loved ones in 1993 when their villages were attacked by Muslim forces and Naser Oric at their head. So it was known that there would be such a development afterward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You just said that Srebrenica was not demilitarised. In this regard, today you said at transcript page 4, lines 21, 22, you stated that Security Resolution was not reasonable. Do you remember having said that? Could you expand -- explain it in a bit further detail why do you think it was unreasonable?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember saying that, and I stand by that personal opinion. It's a personal opinion. The Resolution was not reasonable for the following reasons: Firstly, there is no definition of a protected area. That definition is not recorded anywhere, not such a definition that would give legal basis to that Resolution. Secondly, it is not possible for someone to be protecting an area and yet in that area there are armed individuals and weapons. How, then, can you achieve protection? Finally, and again this was an erroneous attitude, if you ask me, creating a protected area in the middle of a war is an absurdity. Those creating such areas, had they wished to end the war, instead of creating these areas they could have come up with the Dayton Accords already at this point. The matter is the ratio of territory that had by this time been taken by the one side, and the other side was perhaps deemed to be unfavourable by someone. So everything that I've just said is my personal opinion. I would like to underline that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you have frequent contact with Mr. David Harland at that time while you were in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that we were frequently in touch. I met him whenever he came to the mixed military group meetings which I attended in my capacity as liaison officer. But I know he was married in the way that I described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss with Mr. Harland about your impression or opinion on the with -- the Security Resolution, the UN Security Council's Resolution about it being unreasonable?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Whenever I could, I would talk to Mr. Andreev and others, and I would tell them my personal view on the issue, and that is what I'm doing now. My opinion remains unchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Harland testified here at the Tribunal that the -- to the effect that the obligation placed on UNPROFOR to try to deter Serb attacks by all means necessary was not predicated on the Bosnian government previous demilitarisation of the areas. Do you agree with his observation, and was that the reason why you think Security Council Resolution is not reasonable?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with that observation. The agreement was crystal clear, and it was understood that the protected areas must be demilitarised. The agreement is crystal clear about that, entirely unambiguous. No weapons were to remain inside those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Unless there's a question for you from my colleagues, that concludes your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am grateful to you, your Excellency, for underlying this question in relation to Harland. Could we just have P820 briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your point, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here that the Muslims knew what had happened, whereas Harland says that the Bosniaks themselves were not even sure at this point as to what had happened. That's one thing. And the other was to actually bring up the demilitarisation agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I raised a question about Srebrenica vis-a-vis Mr. Harland.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, you have read the question by Ms. Edgerton, page 29, implying that the Muslims knew what had occurred, whereas Harland in his report claims that the Bosniaks had not yet realised what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would not allow the first question. And what is your second point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In answer to your question at page 96, line 5, about the -- demilitarising the protected areas. Defence Exhibit P3 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There is too much background noise for us to be able to hear the witness -- the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat. Could you tell us first what point -- what your point is, what point you are going to raise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just clarify whether it's in fact true that the areas were to be demilitarised or not, and who was in charge of of demilitarising them? This has been challenged but the witness stands by his previous statement. The document shows exactly what the witness said. It is consistent with what the witness said. There is an obligation to demilitarise and pull the weapons out. If we can produce that document. That is the gist of what I'm asking. 1D5356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll allow you to put that question, but subject to the Prosecution may have some question for its cross if necessary. Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was in charge of implementing the demilitarisation agreement in the protected areas, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above all, the Muslim authorities who signed the agreement. As for the control and monitoring of the implementation, that was up to the UN, and they were supposed to confirm that demilitarisation had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. 1D5356. That is the agreement. We need to be looking specifically at item 4. This is page 2 in the Serbian and also page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we have it already our exhibit, Exhibit D135.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a -- were you referring to the agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. This is a telegram containing information about the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's take a look at D135. Is this it, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that's admitted. I wanted to have the telegram admitted, but we can track it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does Article 2 say? Lieutenant-Colonel, Article 2, please. Tell us what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground, the demilitarised zone shall be marked by UNPROFOR by means of boards on which is stated in English, Serbian, and Bosnian, written in Cyrillic and Latin as follows: "Demilitarised zone. Any military operation is strictly forbidden. (Article 60, protocol 1 additional to the Geneva Conventions)."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page, please. Article 3.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Every military or paramilitary unit will have either to withdraw from the demilitarised zone or submit/hand over their weapons, ammunition, mines, and explosives and combat supplies in the demilitarised zones will be handed over/submitted to UNPROFOR."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Than you. Article 4. Can we pull the page up a little, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 4: "UNPROFOR shall take the handed over/submitted weapons into custody. "UNPROFOR shall take the handed over/submitted ammunition into custody separately."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First sentence Article 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "UNPROFOR shall control the demilitarised zone."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we please go back to 1D5356. Lieutenant-Colonel, did this materialise?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with protocol 60, protocol 1, Article 60? What does it envisage in case one of the parties fails to comply?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what protocol you're talking about. I don't have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 2, please. You read about this article based on which the demilitarisation was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the meeting when this agreement was reached. It went on for nearly 48 hours, and we didn't sleep at all. General Mladic asked for Sarajevo to be included in the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please go through Article 4 or item 4 in its entirety. In the Serbian [indiscernible] is the next page but in English it's all on the same page. Does it faithfully convey what was actually agreed at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in full. It requires or demands a full demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who was in charge of carrying this out and performing checks?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the demilitarisation, that would be the signatories. As for monitoring, implementation, that was up to the UN, UNPROFOR specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the last sentence in paragraph 4. The very last sentence of paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO INDJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the completion the demilitarisation process not a single armed person or unit apart from UNPROFOR forces will remain in the town. UNPROFOR is responsible for the demilitarisation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we not admitted this before, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't know, but with Mr. Reid's help, I can advise the parties pretty quickly, I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it then now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2804, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we need to stop here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2143, D2143. It appears to have been admitted. We might as well keep the number in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to ask any questions, Ms. Edgerton, in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, I have no questions whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's correct. We admit it as D2143. So we don't need to admit it separately. Thank you. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Indjic. Thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. With the indulgence of -- you may be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- of the interpreter I need to give this short brief oral ruling now giving the timing. We'll resume on Monday morning. As the Chamber refers to the Rule 92 ter notification for the Witness Milan Mandic and the draft statement which has been uploaded as 65 ter 1D6814. Having reviewed the statement, the Chamber finds that paragraphs 13 and 14 relate to crimes committed against Bosnian Serbs and will not be admitted on the grounds that it is irrelevant. The Chamber orders the accused to upload a redacted version of Milan Mandic's statement to reflect this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can do that, but with respect to this and also Mr. Sehovac, if you don't mind, since we're going to be proofing them on Sunday, we would probably prefer to just instead of redacting this, we'll make those adjustments when we make the final revised statement if that's okay. Otherwise, we'll end up making this -- redacting this and then changing it again. So if you would just be patient, by Monday we will have a revised and final statement for both witnesses that will include the deletions of paragraphs that you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Could you do -- offer a tracked version as well to understand what has been changed?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate the interpreters, court reporters, and everybody's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I -- on behalf of the Tribunal, I have to apologise to Mr. Milosevic for having waited so long in vain. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 28th day of January, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.04 p.m.,
